title: Priyam Raj on building SaaS in your 20s: niche down, own distribution, ship fast and track what changes
summary: A long conversation with two other creators about careers, money and AI in your 20s. Priyam Raj, who built and sold Morise and now runs Vidai, shares how he finds ideas from his own problems, got his first sale via Twitter, and defends SaaS against AI commoditization with niching and distribution.

principles.text: Build tools that solve your own problem; you will be more motivated to finish and the idea is already validated.
principles.quote: You'll be so motivated to solve it too because it's your own problem.

principles.text: Defend a product against AI commoditization by niching down and owning distribution.
principles.quote: I feel the way to defend that in a way would be to niche things down. I think niching things down help helps a lot.

principles.text: If you already have distribution, a product built around your own audience stays defensible even when tools become a chat away.
principles.quote: If you can figure out distribution first, this is definitely going to be a much better take.

principles.text: Find communities of people doing what you want to do; seeing real revenue screenshots makes the goal feel possible.
principles.quote: Try finding communities into things you're enthusiastic about.

principles.text: Get early exposure on Twitter by building in public and engaging with bigger accounts, then tweet when you launch.
principles.quote: I was uh you know uh tweeting out a lot about hey this is what I learned about people who grow on YouTube. So I try to build an audience about it like even if it's very less people

principles.text: In a fast-changing field, track new tools constantly and adopt them early to stay ahead.
principles.quote: You must keep a track of what's changing in the world because tomorrow it can be obsolete
